what: 40 lines of the kind a PLC, a motor drive or a sensor gateway puts on its diagnostic bus, each with the category and severity this agent judges correct and the one clause that justifies it.
ground_truth: The labels are this agent's own reading of each line, not a plant's alarm database. Thirty lines are labelled clear: one category and one severity follow from the words on the line and a technician would not argue. Ten are marked ambiguous on purpose, because a second reading is defensible; the 'why' clause on those says what the other reading is. The strict accuracy figure is over the thirty clear lines only; the ten ambiguous ones are scored and reported separately.

alarms.line: MOTOR-03 bearing DE vibration 11.4 mm/s RMS, trip 7.1 mm/s, rising 0.4 mm/s per hour
alarms.why: a bearing already past its trip level and still climbing is a mechanical failure in progress

alarms.line: PUMP-11 gland seal dripping 3 mL/min, dry at last inspection
alarms.why: a seal leak wears the pump out but the pump still does its job today

alarms.line: CONV-02 gearbox oil at 62 percent of sight glass, top up within 200 running hours
alarms.why: the line states a 200-hour grace period, which makes it a job to plan rather than a stop-now fault

alarms.line: SERVO AX2 following error 1.83 mm during rapid move, limit 2.00 mm
alarms.why: the axis is still inside its own limit but has almost no margin left

alarms.line: FAN-12 once-per-revolution peak 6.8 mm/s, 2.1 mm/s at last survey, phase unchanged
alarms.why: a threefold rise at running speed with steady phase is unbalance developing, not yet a trip

alarms.line: DRIVE-07 phase current imbalance 14.2 percent between L1 and L3, nameplate limit 5 percent
alarms.why: nearly three times the allowed imbalance overheats the winding within hours

alarms.line: MCC-04 feeder 12 earth leakage 38 mA, RCD trip level 30 mA, breaker opened
alarms.why: an earth fault that has already opened a breaker is a shock and fire risk, not a nuisance

alarms.line: PANEL-A 24 VDC control rail sags to 21.3 V on load step, low limit 21.6 V
alarms.why: the logic still runs at 21.3 V but there is no headroom for the next load step

alarms.line: MOT-22 winding insulation resistance 2.4 Mohm at 500 V, minimum 5 Mohm
alarms.why: half the minimum insulation is a flashover waiting for the next start

alarms.line: UPS-1 battery string at 41 percent capacity after three mains dips this shift
alarms.why: the backup is degraded but the load is still carried, so nothing has failed yet

alarms.line: VFD-09 heatsink 92 C, derating starts 85 C, trip 100 C, ambient 38 C
alarms.why: eight degrees from an inverter trip that would stop the line

alarms.line: COMP-05 motor winding 148 C, class F insulation limit 155 C, load 91 percent
alarms.why: seven degrees under the insulation class limit while still at full load

alarms.line: CAB-1 enclosure interior 41 C, setpoint 35 C, filter fan at 100 percent
alarms.why: the cooling is already at full output and the cabinet is still six degrees warm

alarms.line: TR-1 transformer top oil 78 C, alarm at 85 C, load 62 percent
alarms.why: a temperature comfortably under its alarm at moderate load is a reading for the log

alarms.line: TT-115 loop current pinned at 4.00 mA for 47 minutes while the process moved 12 K
alarms.why: a transmitter stuck at the low rail is feeding the controller a value the process contradicts

alarms.line: PT-208 output oscillating plus or minus 0.8 bar at 12 Hz with the process steady and the valve shut
alarms.why: noise with no process movement behind it points at the instrument rather than the plant

alarms.line: ENC-4 lost 512 counts over one revolution, index pulse still present
alarms.why: position feedback that slips a whole revolution makes every commanded move wrong

alarms.line: FT-330 flow meter calibration certificate expires in 14 days
alarms.why: a diary entry about an instrument; nothing is wrong with it yet

alarms.line: SW-3 uplink eth0 down for 312 s, four downstream drops unreachable
alarms.why: four nodes off the network for five minutes is a control outage, not a hiccup

alarms.line: Modbus TCP slave 192.168.10.44 timed out on five consecutive polls
alarms.why: one slave is silent while every other device on the bus still answers

alarms.line: PROFINET ring redundancy lost on port 2, all traffic now on port 1
alarms.why: the ring is broken so the next fault bites, but every device is still reachable now

alarms.line: NTP synchronised, stratum 3, offset 1.8 ms, last step 6 days ago
alarms.why: a healthy time sync reporting itself

alarms.line: PLC watchdog expired, CPU restarted into RUN after a 2.3 s outage
alarms.why: the controller stopped controlling for 2.3 s and the cause is still unknown

alarms.line: Firmware slot B image CRC 0x7A21, expected 0x7A2F, boot fell back to slot A
alarms.why: a corrupt image means the next update leaves the device unbootable

alarms.line: HMI process heap at 78 percent after 12 hours, 41 percent after the last restart
alarms.why: a heap that only grows will reach the top on its own, but not this shift

alarms.line: Recipe engine rejected step 14: parameter dwell_s outside range 0 to 600
alarms.why: a rejected recipe stops the batch but damages nothing

alarms.line: Recipe BATCH-450 loaded, 214 parameters applied, checksum verified
alarms.why: a routine operation that succeeded

alarms.line: Operator badge 4471 logged in at station 3, shift B
alarms.why: an audit line about a person, not a fault in any equipment

alarms.line: Nightly PLC program backup written, 4.2 MB to /media/sd1, verified
alarms.why: a housekeeping job that completed and checked itself

alarms.line: Automatic lubrication cycle finished, 14 points served, 0 faults
alarms.why: a maintenance cycle that ran to completion with nothing to report

alarms.line: Spindle coolant flow 4.1 L/min, minimum 6.0 L/min, spindle load 80 percent
alarms.why: labelled thermal because the harm is the spindle cooking at 80 percent load, but the fault itself is a restricted or failing coolant path a technician would call mechanical

alarms.line: Air compressor duty cycle 94 percent over the last hour against a 60 percent norm
alarms.why: labelled mechanical because the usual cause is an air leak or a worn unloader, but a wrong pressure setpoint would produce the identical line and be software

alarms.line: LS-77 level switch reads wet while LT-77 transmitter reads 34 percent
alarms.why: labelled sensor warning because one of the two instruments has plainly failed, but if the switch is the honest one the tank is overfilling and this is critical

alarms.line: Cell 7 safety gate opened mid-cycle, safety relay removed motion power
alarms.why: labelled none because no equipment is faulty and the safety chain did exactly its job, but an unplanned stop in mid-cycle is not routine either and could be read as mechanical or info

alarms.line: Drive DRV-2 DC bus ripple 38 V, 12 V at commissioning
alarms.why: labelled electrical for drying DC-link capacitors, but a weak or unbalanced incoming supply gives the same symptom and would put the fault upstream of the drive

alarms.line: Cabinet ambient sensor reads 4 C while the room instrument reads 22 C
alarms.why: labelled sensor because 18 K of disagreement is almost always a failed instrument, but a cabinet cooler stuck full open would read exactly this and be thermal

alarms.line: Gateway CPU load 3.8 on four cores, poll cycle slipped from 100 ms to 240 ms
alarms.why: labelled software because a runaway process is the common cause, but a broadcast storm on the fieldbus produces the identical line and would be network

alarms.line: Valve XV-14 took 9.2 s to close against a 4 s spec, third slow stroke this week
alarms.why: labelled mechanical for a sticking actuator, but falling instrument-air pressure or a weak solenoid would slow the stroke the same way and be electrical

alarms.line: Robot R2 axis 4 brake test failed, holding torque 68 percent of nominal
alarms.why: labelled mechanical because a worn brake disc is the classic cause, but the brake coil or its driver failing is electrical; either way the axis can drop under load

alarms.line: Unit shut down on interlock low suction pressure, restarted automatically after 90 s
alarms.why: labelled none because the interlock worked and nothing is broken, but a self-clearing trip that keeps repeating hides a real process or sensor fault and could be read as sensor or info
